/pages/8/summary: Here you find understandable explanations for preparing your project. You learn which information helps and how a first idea becomes an agreed scope.
/pages/8/sections/0/body: Here you find understandable explanations for preparing your project. You learn which information helps and how a first idea becomes an agreed scope.
/pages/8/sections/1/body: Before anything is built, we sort out your need, the systems involved and a verifiable goal. Knowledge is not an end in itself here: it serves to record the task, scope and acceptance criteria so that progress stays verifiable. You receive an understandable assessment instead of jargon.
/pages/8/sections/2/body: Our knowledge base (Brain) links content with origin, date and scope. This makes it possible at any time to check what a statement is based on. Customer data and general knowledge stay separate; nothing is mixed or adopted unchecked. Open points are marked as open.
/pages/8/sections/3/body: A short description of the goal, examples of existing processes and notes on systems to be connected are helpful. The more concrete the user journey, the more precise the proposal. A first conversation or a draft quote stays non-binding until separately approved.
/pages/8/metadata/description: Here you find understandable explanations for preparing your project. You learn which information helps and how a first idea becomes an agreed scope.
/pages/9/summary: Note your goal, the people involved and the existing systems. Describe a concrete path from the first contact to the desired result. Together we clarify the right scope from this.
/pages/9/sections/0/body: Note your goal, the people involved and the existing systems. Describe a concrete path from the first contact to the desired result. Together we clarify the right scope from this.
/pages/9/sections/1/body: Describe what should work better in the end: less manual work, faster answers, a clearer overview. A goal in one sentence helps more than a long wish list. From this we jointly derive a verifiable scope.
/pages/9/sections/2/body: Which systems, inboxes, spreadsheets or portals are in use today? What works, what gets in the way? This inventory prevents duplicate work and shows where a connection makes sense and where a new build does.
/pages/9/sections/3/heading: Step 3: Choose the right entry point
/pages/9/sections/3/body: For a public presence you start with websites, for recurring enquiries and appointments with agents and automation, for protected overviews with apps and portals. Which parts belong together is clarified along the concrete user journey – without committing to prices that are not approved.
